skill.name: deployment-procedures
skill.description: Production deployment guidance for safe releases, verification, rollback planning, and emergency response across common hosting platforms.
skill.summary: Plan safer production releases with deployment checks, rollback decisions, and post-release verification.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences used for diagrams. I found no evidence of prompt injection, malicious intent, or executable deployment scripts in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 28 starts a plain markdown diagram for platform selection. It contains no Ruby backtick expression, shell command, user input, or executable instruction.
Line 43 closes the markdown diagram and is followed by explanatory deployment tables. No command execution pattern or injection path is present.
Line 85 starts a markdown workflow diagram for prepare, backup, deploy, verify, and rollback phases. It is documentation text, not executable shell syntax.

content.value_statement: Production releases can fail when teams skip checks, backups, or rollback planning. This skill gives practical deployment principles, verification steps, and emergency decisions.
actual_capabilities: Helps choose deployment approaches for static sites, web apps, microservices, serverless, Docker, and Kubernetes.
Provides pre-deployment checks for tests, builds, environment variables, backups, rollback plans, and monitoring.
Explains a five-phase deployment workflow: prepare, backup, deploy, verify, and confirm or rollback.
Lists post-deployment verification checks for health endpoints, logs, user flows, and performance.
Compares rollback methods and zero-downtime strategies for common platforms.
limitations: Does not provide complete platform-specific command scripts.
Does not replace production access controls, change approval, or incident response ownership.
Requires users to adapt guidance to their infrastructure, compliance needs, and release tooling.
Does not validate live environments or execute deployments.

use_cases.title: Prepare a release checklist
use_cases.description: Create a practical checklist before deploying a web application to production.

use_cases.title: Review rollback readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether backups, rollback steps, monitoring, and team communication are ready before a release.

use_cases.title: Select a deployment strategy
use_cases.description: Compare rolling, blue-green, and canary options for a high-risk production change.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic deployment checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a production deployment checklist for my app. Include tests, build checks, backups, rollback planning, and monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Assess release readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned deployment using this skill. Identify missing checks, rollback risks, monitoring gaps, and team communication steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan rollback and verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design rollback triggers, verification windows, health checks, and post-deployment monitoring for this release.

prompt_templates.title: Compare advanced release strategies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare rolling, blue-green, and canary deployment strategies for my change. Recommend one with risks and verification steps.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy a small web app today.
output: Recommended approach: use your platform deployment flow with active monitoring open.
Before deployment: confirm tests, production build, environment variables, backup, rollback path, and team notice.
After deployment: check health endpoint, error logs, key user flows, and performance for the first 15 minutes.

output_examples.input: Our release changes authentication and database schema.
output: Risk level: high because login and data structure are affected.
Recommended strategy: stage first, confirm backup, define rollback triggers, and deploy during a staffed window.
Verification focus: login, signup, password reset, database migration state, error logs, and response time.

output_examples.input: The service is down after deployment.
output: Immediate action: assess the visible symptom and check whether a quick restart is safe.
If the symptom remains unclear or severe, rollback first and investigate after service stability returns.
Communicate status, record the timeline, and review root cause after recovery.

best_practices: Deploy small changes with a clear rollback plan and active monitoring.
Verify tests, builds, environment variables, backups, and team communication before release.
Review logs, health checks, user flows, and performance after deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy without a tested rollback path.
Do not combine unrelated changes in one risky release.
Do not leave immediately after production deployment.

faq.question: Does this skill run deployment commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides deployment principles, checklists, and decision support. Users must adapt steps to their own platform.

faq.question: Which platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It discusses static hosting, managed web apps, VPS deployments, Docker, Kubernetes, serverless, and edge functions.

faq.question: Can it help with rollbacks?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains rollback triggers, platform-specific rollback concepts, and verification after recovery.

faq.question: Is this useful for zero-downtime releases?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares rolling, blue-green, and canary strategies for different release risks.

faq.question: Does it replace an incident response process?
faq.answer: No. It supports deployment thinking, but teams still need owners, access controls, escalation paths, and live monitoring.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
